producer_report.summary: Both snapshot locks (Snapshot::lock in athena-git, lock in athena-core) now call one shared routine, athena_git::snapshot::writable_paths. It attempts a real write at every directory (creates and removes .athena-lock-probe) and every regular file (opens for append), root and .git included, symlinks skipped. Findings split into `accepted` (write worked) and `unchecked` (could not be tried: not listable, not a regular file, other error). WriteFindings::refusal builds the error with separate wording for each and paths relative to the root. A lock with any finding is undone and refused. Both old two-place probe_write functions are gone. Each lock is split into a private lock_with(.., after_apply) test seam; the public lock passes a no-op. Tests use the real unlock_dir on one empty leaf directory so they bind root. Added a CHANGELOG Fixed entry, and a decision entry D167 with a decision-links.toml link, because D08 governs athena-git's snapshot.rs. verification.rs and run_pin_tests.rs were left unchanged (out of scope per the reading; they need no compile fix).

checks_run.note: 18 tests, including the four new ones
13 tests incl. the new evidence-lock test and the run_pin_tests rerun tests
decision log and link checks, 14 tests

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`: a new test leaves one nested path (e.g. .git/objects) writable in an otherwise locked tree, constructed so it binds root too (attempted write or injected writable path, not mode bits alone), and asserts `Snapshot::lock` returns an error naming exactly that path. It fails against the old two-place probe.
criteria_check.evidence: a_lock_with_one_nested_path_left_writable_is_refused_naming_it passes: creates .git/objects/leaf, locks for real, reopens that one leaf with the real unlock_dir via the lock_with hook, asserts the Refused text contains `.git/objects/leaf` with exactly two backticks. The old probe (root file + .git/HEAD) would see only locked paths, so lock_with would return Ok and expect_err would panic. Ran as root here.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test in crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs does the same for the evidence-snapshot `lock`, asserting the error names the nested writable path, and it fails against the old probe when run as root.
criteria_check.evidence: an_evidence_lock_with_one_nested_path_left_writable_is_refused_naming_it passes in cargo test -p athena-core: reopens records/a/leaf with the real unlock_dir after the lock, asserts 'evidence snapshot lock does not hold' and `records/a/leaf` with two backticks. The old probe tried only the root and history.json so it would pass the lock.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs `lock` calls the shared athena-git routine, and its own `probe_write` is deleted (Grep finds no `fn probe_write` there); athena-git's `lock` uses the same routine over every directory and file including .git.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep for `fn probe_write` under crates/ finds 0 matches. core lock_with calls athena_git::snapshot::writable_paths(dir); Snapshot::lock_with calls writable_paths(&self.dir). Test writable_paths_tries_a_write_at_every_directory_and_file asserts the accepted list holds the root, .git, .git/objects, .git/HEAD and src/main.rs.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`: a test shows that after a successful `lock()` then `unlock()` no `.athena-lock-probe` file exists anywhere in the tree and the work-tree tree hash equals its value before the lock.
criteria_check.evidence: a_lock_then_unlock_leaves_no_probe_file_and_the_tree_unchanged passes: real lock() then unlock(), walks the whole tree including .git for LOCK_PROBE, compares work_tree_tree() with the earlier value; repeats after writable_paths on the unlocked tree.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`: a test shows the lock error text differs between a path that accepted a write and a path that could not be checked (e.g. 'could not be listed').
criteria_check.evidence: the_lock_error_text_differs_for_an_accepted_write_and_an_unchecked_path passes: a writable file gives 'a write was accepted at `file.txt`' without 'could not be checked'; a Unix socket gives 'could not be checked: `sock` (not a regular file)'; the two texts differ. The 'could not be listed' wording exists in the code but cannot be forced as root, so the socket case is used.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git` and `cargo test -p athena-core`: existing tests still pass, including `a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree` and the snapshot-change rerun tests in run_pin_tests.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test --locked -q -p athena-git -p athena-core: all pass (1229 passed, 1 ignored in core, 0 failed); a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree ok in the athena-git run; the run_pin_tests rerun tests ok in the athena-core run.

open_issues: The 'could not be listed' error text is built in code but has no direct test, because root can list any directory; the socket case covers the unchecked path in general.
A special file (socket, fifo, device) anywhere in a snapshot now fails the lock. Git checkout never writes such files, so this is the fail-closed choice.
The new tests were not run against the old source; the failing-before claim rests on the code (the old probe checked only the root and one file).
learnings: D08 governs crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs, so a change there needs a new docs/decisions.md entry plus a [[link]] in docs/decision-links.toml whose `line` is the line of the 'Amends D08' phrase in the new entry.
As root, a directory cannot be made unlistable, so the 'could not be listed' wording cannot be tested; a Unix socket exercises the unchecked path.
unlock_dir on a single nested leaf clears chattr +i there, so it makes a clean seam for reopening exactly one path under a locked parent.
desires: A way to run the new tests against the old source to show they fail there; I argued it from the code instead.
